newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher, propped up by CBOT rally.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher, propped up by CBOT rally.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher and well above session lows on spillover support from a rally in CBOT wheat, traders said.
But KCBT wheat ended weaker than its counterpart in Chicago amid a liquidation of long positions in the nearby December contract.
"You should see a big drop in open interest in the Dec contract tomorrow moring," a KCBT trader said.
KCBT wheat saw pressure after the CCC amended a tender to buy wheat for Bangladesh. CCC originally sought only HRW wheat but added soft wheat varieties to the tender options.
An apparent softening of basis levels for hard red winter wheat at the Gulf also pressured KCBT wheat.
"The market's tired. We're getting close to seeing some wheat move in the country and there's also the realization that world prices have stabilized," a trader said in early midsession dealings.
KCBT wheat closed 1-1/2 to five cents higher, with December up 2-1/2 cents at $4.35 a bushel. December/March spread closed at 29 cents after trading as wide as 30 cents.

Traders said General Mills bull-spread 2.5 million Dec/March at 29 to 29-1/2 cents. FIMAT and CIS each bull-spread 1.7 million Dec/March from 28-1/2 to 30 cents. Prudential and Chicago Corp each bear-spread 1.2 million March/Dec from 29 to 30 cents.
In flat price activity, CIS sold 3.2 March bushels and Benson-Quinn sold 1.2 million Dec bushels.
